columns:
Management of risks and opportunities linked to
ESG.
This includes measures taken to preserve or
restore the environment and ensure compliance
with global best practice in good governance.
It further extends to actions aimed at promoting,
protecting and ensuring the effective exercise of
human and other rights needed to underwrite
sustainable development across society.

Reduce the Bank’s and its
value chain’s negative impacts
on society and environment.
Implement restorative
programmes.
Contribute to societal growth
through community
development projects and
financial inclusion and literacy
initiatives.
Promote transparency,
accountability and ethical
behaviour.

Potential for negative ESG
impact resulting from the
Bank’s operations/actions.
Financing of clients/activities
/sectors that have a negative
impact on the environment
and violate human rights.
Adverse impact of supply
chain on the environment and
society.

Portfolio exposure to
sectors with adverse
environmental impact.
Slow transition of at-risk
portfolio exposures.
Depreciation and early
retirement of existing
assets (damage to property
and assets in "high risk"
locations).
Greenwashing that may
have adverse impact on the
brand and erode investor
confidence.

Sustainability linked
financial products.
Financing of new portfolios
and/or activities linked to
sustainability.
Access to new sources of
capital from sustainable
financiers.
Thought leadership:
sustainable innovations.
Operational cost savings
due to improved efficiency
in resource use.
